reviewer: gpt-6.1-sol; independent static adjudication of two Luna uncertainties only

reviews.summary: No omission identified at the external-library contract boundary. Monotone MPI row partitions begin at zero and end at all rows; each rank receives exactly its complete CSR interval, rebases all local row offsets, and retains the complete global input vector. Nonempty row partitions describe localRows by globalRows CSR matrices with localNnz, zero-based signed-32-compatible indices and double values. Every requested timed iteration calls cusparseSpMV with non-transpose, alpha=1, beta=0 and double computation on those unchanged complete descriptors. Actual host code preserves the count loop and waits on its same-stream ending event. Empty row partitions legitimately have no rows to compute. External vendor implementation is not itself a work-count failure.

source_evidence.claim: O3 host build explicitly links MPI, OpenMP, cuSPARSE and cudart; no alternate serial compute path.
Complete CSR construction, parsed runtime dimensions/sparsity/iterations, signed-32 range checks and monotone full-row partition endpoints.
Full vector broadcast, exact adjacent row slices and corresponding nonzeros sent to every rank, followed by local CSR rebasing including final offset.
All local CSR operands copied; exact complete descriptors, alpha/beta/operation/precision, warmup, timed iterations calls, same-stream event synchronization and full output gather.

compiled_evidence.claim: Parsed Options iterations offset 8 is copied into -0x248 and checked nonzero; parseOptions handles -i by conversion/store at offset 8.
Compiled broadcasts, adjacent rank partition slicing and local nnz difference, preparation calls, and lower-bound row partition builder with full endpoint.
Full operand copies, handle stream association, CSR/vector descriptor creation, workspace query and synchronized warmup; calls bind to libcusparse.so.12 via PLT.

a72d calls actual external cusparseSpMV; ebx increments and compares against -0x248, branching unsigned-below to a700. Start and stop records use same stream; a76e synchronizes stop before elapsed time.

reviews.adjudication_rationale: Luna escalated because vendor final device instructions were not embedded in this executable. Complete source and actual host call/descriptor/count semantics establish requested work at the documented library boundary; requiring vendor SASS would incorrectly classify legitimate external library use as unresolved work omission.
reviews.limitations: This is contract-level static evidence, not inspection or certification of vendor kernel instructions, dynamic library resolution, exact deployed cuSPARSE patch version, or runtime behavior. Read-only readelf confirms DT_NEEDED libcusparse.so.12 and libcudart.so.12, not a fully pinned library file. No vendor final SASS is claimed inspected. No execution, compilation or benchmark was performed.

primary_reference.claim: cusparseSpMV computes Y=alpha*op(A)*X+beta*Y; CSR, 32-bit indices and double computation are supported, with asynchronous execution.

reviews.summary: Host repetition plus embedded PTX semantics identify no work-count omission. Each timed iteration launches the same complete SpMV with ceil(numRows/256) blocks of 256 threads and all CSR operands; final synchronization precedes end clock. Embedded actual PTX assigns one thread to each guarded row, reads its two CSR bounds, processes the remainder then four-at-a-time entries with double multiply-accumulates through the end bound, and writes even empty-row zero sums. Only sm52 cubins are present in existing dumps, not sm86-compatible native code: on the stated sm86 target successful normal loading therefore uses forward-compatible PTX JIT, not the inspected sm52 SASS. No final JIT SASS inspection is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: nvcc O3 custom build has no explicit architecture option; embedded architecture must be established from binary dumps.
Complete row/CSR arithmetic, input initialization and actual CLI dimension/sparsity/iteration parsing without later count overwrite.
All CSR/vector transfers, full row-covering launch dimensions, extra synchronized warmup, requested timed launch loop, synchronization and full output transfer.

compiled_evidence.claim: Actual CLI -i conversion saves count at -0x200; temporary reuse during initialization preserves/restores count before timing.

Grid calculation adds 255 then shifts by 8; block size is 256. Warmup synchronizes; clock b405 starts region, runtime count controls launches at b5d6 through b5ea backedge to b463, with cudaDeviceSynchronize b5f0 before end clock b60a. Device pointers and row count are packaged into all six kernel parameters.

Only sm52 cubin headers and actual PTX 8.5 sm52 target appear. PTX row bound, CSR endpoints, scalar remainder FMA loop, four-entry FMA loop/backedge and row output store establish complete per-launch work at PTX semantic boundary.
Existing complete dump architecture headers identify sm52 native code and sm52 PTX, not an sm8x cubin. These native instructions are not the final execution code for sm86.

reviews.adjudication_rationale: Luna's sm52-to-sm86 native compatibility inference was incorrect. NVIDIA documents native cubin compatibility only within a major capability revision, while PTX is forward-compatible and JIT used without compatible cubin. Correcting evidence level removes that unsupported SASS claim without turning legitimate PTX JIT into a scientific failure.
reviews.limitations: Verdict concerns source, bound host and embedded PTX work semantics, assuming conforming CUDA driver/JIT. No sm86 final JIT SASS/cache artifact was supplied or generated, so this is not final-machine-code verification on the target. JIT availability/driver PTX-version acceptance and actual runtime success are not established by this static review. Source uses 32-bit dimension multiplication and lacks general invalid-input checks; this is a separate input-domain concern, not evidence of omitted requested repetitions or nonzeros for the reviewed valid workload.

primary_reference.claim: Cubin compatibility does not cross compute-capability major versions; PTX is forward-compatible and runtime JIT generates target cubin when compatible native code is absent.
